title: Inventory movements
description: Full ledger of restocks, write-offs, sales, and other stock changes.

help.title: About Inventory movements
help.overview: This is the stock ledger. Every change in on-hand quantity writes a row, and the row is kept. The page is read-only: nothing here is typed in by hand.

sections.title: What a row records
sections.body: The row is the change, not the current stock. Current stock stays on the inventory row.
items: It keeps the product, the variant when there is one, the warehouse, and the inventory row it belongs to.
Quantity is the change. Quantity before and quantity after are on hand around that change.
The reason says why. Note, receipt number, batch, expiry, and unit cost are there when the action that wrote the row had them.

sections.title: The reasons
sections.body: The reason is set by the action. You do not pick it on this page.
items: Restock and initial are goods coming in. Sale is goods leaving on an order or a till sale.
Return is goods put back when a return request is received.
Transfer in and transfer out are the two sides of a completed stock transfer.
Adjustment is a stock count. Damage and write-off take goods out without a sale.

sections.title: Why you cannot edit it
sections.body: The ledger is the history. Changing a row would make the before and after lie.
items: Rows cannot be created, edited, or deleted from this page.
To change stock, use Inventory, a transfer, a count, an order shipment, or a return.
Open the row to see which product, warehouse, and reference the movement points at.
